problem:
The second-order differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+{e}^{t}{y}^{′}+2ty={t}^{2}
$$

can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}={x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}^{′}=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${x}_{1}(t)=y(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)={y}^{′}(t).$ Find the function $f(t).$

Question 1

The second-order differential equation y″+ety′+2ty=t2 can be written as a system of first-order differential equations, as follows: {x1′=x2x2′=f(t) where x1(t)=y(t) and x2(t)=y′(t). Find the function f(t).

a
−2tx1−etx2+t2
b
−2etx1−t2x2+t
c
2etx1+tx2−t2
d
2tx1+etx2−t2
e
−t2x1+etx2+t
